test_policy.notes: Lewis is test-optional for first-year applicants for all programs, with the same consideration for admission and merit scholarships (scores, if sent, are also used in the scholarship review). Test-optional applicants submit a personal statement or graded school assignment. Official scores are requested before registration for course placement. The international page lists no SAT/ACT requirement.

requirements.notes: International first-year documents: application, secondary transcripts or national exam results, secondary school completion certificate, English proficiency scores, passport copy; then an affidavit of support for the I-20. Holistic review focuses on cumulative and core GPA and course rigor; recommendations are optional. No application fee amount is stated on the pages reviewed.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Applicants whose previous education was taught primarily in English may be exempt: citizens of countries on Lewis's waiver list need no test; others can combine IGCSE/A Level or IB results with an ACT or SAT score, or submit an ESL graduation certificate from a partner school (ELS, Kaplan, LaSallian Language Center, local community colleges). U.S.-based transfer students with a degree or two college English courses may be waived. Lewis may test English on arrival and place students in support courses.

english.notes: The page gives no minimum on the new 1-6 TOEFL scale.

aid.notes: International undergraduate scholarships are based on previous-school GPA converted to a U.S. 4.0 scale and are calculated automatically after the application and documents are in; the tuition page says up to $18,000 per year for full-time students at the Romeoville campus (the international overview says '$17K maximum'). Lewis says merit scholarships are awarded regardless of citizenship. No need-based aid for international students is described; Mpower no-cosigner loans are available.
